description:
FILED s540e (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-15) while building #4991.  Probe scratch/s540e/probe/strf.pl (+ strfcmp.pl, a per-letter comparer) in the s540e worktree: 4 zones x 20 dates x 41 letters + isdst rows.  The s540e tree answers every one of these exactly as the base 75904a35 does (strf.base = strf.tree); the one row s540e changed is the DST-gap shift (fixed: posix-01.t row 18).

Per letter, perl vs PCL (unset TZ = the box's EET, perl's LC_TIME = the box's English locale):
- %c: perl "Thu 01 Jan 1970 12:00:00 AM EET" (80 of 80 rows), PCL asctime's "Thu Jan  1 00:00:00 1970".  %x: perl "01/01/1970", PCL "01/01/70".  %X: perl "12:00:00 AM", PCL "00:00:00".  These are LC_TIME's -- under LC_ALL=C perl gives the C forms (measure; PCL answers the C locale always: the POSIX shim's setlocale story).
- %Z: perl the zone ABBREVIATION (EET, EEST, EDT, UTC, BMT), PCL "UTC+02" / "UTC+03".
- %z: perl EMPTY when isdst is -1 (the default) -- a 5.40 quirk of ints_to_tm? -- and "+0200" with an explicit isdst; PCL always the offset.
- %G %g %V: 4 rows differ, e.g. 1970-01-01 (Thursday): perl 1970 / 70 / 01, PCL 1969 / 69 / 52 (`_iso_week`'s year-start arm).
- isdst 0 / 1: perl's %s moves by an hour (mktime with the flag); PCL ignores the argument.
- %s at 1900-01-01: perl -2208995064 (Bucharest LMT +1:44:24), PCL -2208996000.
- strftime('100%', ...): perl "100%", PCL dies "unimplemented conversion %".
- strftime('%Y', 0, 0, 0): perl dies (usage), check PCL.

BAR: each fixed letter probed perl -> base -> tree under two zones and LC_ALL=C; rows in Pl/t/posix-01.t.  The locale letters need a ruling (C locale always vs perl's LC_TIME).
subject: PRE-EXISTING (s540e, probed): POSIX::strftime diverges from perl 5.40.3 in the LOCALE letters (%c %x %X follow perl's LC_TIME: "Thu 01 Jan 1970 12:00:00 AM EET", "01/01/1970", "12:00:00 AM"), the zone letters (%Z is the abbreviation EET / EEST in perl, "UTC+02" in PCL; %z is EMPTY in perl when isdst < 0), the ISO week at a year start (%G/%g/%V of 1970-01-01: perl 1970-W01, PCL 1969-W52), the isdst argument (ignored), %s for pre-1900 local mean time, and a lone trailing `%` (perl prints it, PCL dies)
